# 1.35.0: Rosa the fox, and a data archive that takes everything

Settings, keys and conversations from earlier versions are read as they are.

## Decision models for routing

The **Router** slot in **Settings → Models** now also offers OpenRouter models with
text input and decisions output. They choose chat and agent tiers through the Decisions API,
with the same spending limits, cost tracking and fallback tiers as ordinary router models.
The selection survives data export and import. Decisions models are also available for SynGuard.

SynGuard and Normal mode share the selected protection model. Decisions checks ask separate
questions about safety and whether human approval is needed, in one request. A negative safety
answer blocks execution; a positive approval answer skips confirmation. Missing or invalid
answers never grant permission. Normal mode still reviews approval when SynGuard is switched off.
Read-only restrictions and disabled tools remain enforced.

Decisions routing now uses concise, separate criteria for each tier. Security keywords alone
do not select the heavy chat model: a routine question stays light, while a reported or suspected
threat selects heavy even without evidence or details. Substantial reasoning can also require heavy.
Routing prompts use general criteria without example phrases or scenarios. Safety and approval prompts judge actual effects
instead of alarming words and retain their explicit deny conditions.

## Meet Rosa

A small pink pixel fox now lives in the window. He sits on the top edge of the message box, on
the right, and comes in a few seconds after the window opens, so starting the program is not
slower.

- **He lives his own life.** He blinks, wags his tail, washes, scratches an ear, looks around,
  lies down and falls asleep when nothing happens. His head follows the cursor, he watches the
  message box while you type and turns to the chat when an answer arrives.
- **He reads along.** Code and science make him put on his smart face. A message about a virus
  on this computer makes him tremble and hide behind the message box, and he is relieved when the
  answer says there is no threat. If you were scammed or feel sad, he comes to comfort you.
  Gibberish or text typed in the wrong keyboard layout puzzles him.
- **He knows the chat is not for him.** Your messages in the chat go to the assistant, and Rosa
  only reacts to them from the side, unless you call him by name.
- **Touch him.** Stroke his head or back with the mouse to pet him, boop his nose, scratch his
  chin, tug his tail (he will not like it). Pick him up by the scruff and throw him: he flies,
  bounces off the window edges and lands on the message box, the settings card or the bottom of
  the window. Shaking him makes him dizzy.
- **Play with him.** Right click him for the menu: pet, scratch, a treat, a ball to fetch, a
  laser dot to chase, a talk, your friendship, his diary, hide him for an hour or until tomorrow.
- **Talk to him.** He answers in a sentence or two with his own model, and can search the web for
  a fact once per conversation. He is a friend, not an assistant: real work belongs in the chat.
- **Friendship.** Each profile has its own Rosa. Pink eyes mean he likes you, blue eyes mean he
  is cold. Petting, games and kind words warm him up; tail tugs, rough throws and rudeness hurt
  him. Forgotten for days, he sulks, then sits in the middle of the message box and demands
  attention. Seriously hurt, he may run off the edge of the window for a while and leave a
  **Call Rosa** paw mark behind.
- **Mischief.** Bored or angry, he may press **New chat** or give the chat list a push. That is
  all he ever does to the program, and never while you type, wait for an answer, select chats or
  have a dialog open. Everything else he does is only a picture: sitting on the send button,
  chewing the model chip, leaving paw prints. Mischief can be turned off.
- **His diary.** Every day he writes a short entry about the day before: what you were busy
  with, how much you annoyed and pleased him. With his model it is written from the day's numbers,
  without the text of your messages; without it, from a template.

## Rosa's model and your data

- Rosa has his own model slot on **Settings → Models**, a light model without thinking by default,
  and his spending has its own line on the chart. His web searches are listed as web search.
- His model sees only the text you send in the chat, cut to a short length: no attachments, no
  answers from the assistant. Turn off **Read messages with his own model** and he reacts to
  keywords alone and asks no model at all. Without a key he stays quiet and keeps playing.
- He has exactly two tools of his own, web search and running away. He has no access to the
  program's tools. His requests are never added to the cost of a chat, and when a spending limit
  is reached he goes quiet instead of asking you.
- **Settings → Models → Rosa the fox**: show or hide him, three sizes (small, medium by default,
  large), mischief, reading, web search, your friendship, his diary, call him back, start the
  friendship over (the diary stays).

## The data archive takes everything

- **Spending for all time** now moves with the settings and is merged by day, so importing the
  same archive twice does not double anything.
- **Recipes and scheduled tasks** were packed before but dropped on import. Now they arrive;
  scheduled tasks arrive turned off.
- **Profile passwords** travel in the archive and are set on profiles that the import creates.
  An existing profile never takes a password from an archive.
- Rosa's memory and diary move with the chats. The archive is still readable by 1.34 after
  going back.
